questions.question: The novel ‘God of Small Things’ is a creation of which novelist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The novel **'God of Small Things'** is written by **Arundhati Roy**.
 
• It was first published in **1997** and won the **Booker Prize** in the same year.
 
• The novel is set in the state of **Kerala, India**, and explores the social issues and class relations in Indian society.
 
• 'God of Small Things' is known for its rich prose and intricate narrative structure.
 
• Arundhati Roy is also recognized for her work as an **activist and essayist**, addressing various social and political issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arundhati Roy** was born on **24th November 1961** in Shillong, Meghalaya, India.
 
• Besides her literary work, she is noted for her activism on issues such as **environmentalism and human rights**.
 
• Her other notable works include **'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness'**, **'Field Notes on Democracy'**, and **'Capitalism: A Ghost Story'**.
 
• Roy's writing often addresses themes of **inequality, injustice, and the impact of globalization on local communities**.
 
• Her contributions to literature and social causes have made her a prominent figure both in India and internationally.

questions.question: Which of the following terms best describes the average number of runs a batter makes per 100 deliveries in cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Strike rate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Strike rate** is the term that best describes the average number of runs a batter makes per 100 deliveries in cricket.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the total runs scored by the batter by the number of balls faced, and then multiplying by 100.
 
• The strike rate provides an indication of the scoring efficiency of the batter.
 
• A higher strike rate indicates a more aggressive and faster scoring rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economy rate** is a term used for bowlers, indicating the average number of runs conceded per over.
 
• **Batting average** is the total number of runs scored divided by the number of times the batter has been out.
 
• Both **batting rate** and **batting average** are different metrics used to evaluate a batter's performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty listed in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To engage in political activities to promote democracy
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To engage in political activities to promote democracy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2** is not a fundamental duty listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The fundamental duties are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Constitution.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• They include duties like upholding the sovereignty and integrity of India, preserving the rich heritage, and safeguarding public property.
 
• Engaging in political activities to promote democracy is not listed as a fundamental duty in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental duties** serve as a constant reminder to citizens to build a free, responsible, and healthy society.
 
• There are currently **11 fundamental duties** listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, they are considered vital for the harmonious functioning of the Indian democracy.

questions.question: As of 2022, 12-feet statue of Adi Shankaracharya, which was unveiled by the Prime Minister of India is located in _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kedarnath**__

__
 
• A 12-feet statue of Adi Shankaracharya was unveiled by the Prime Minister of India in **Kedarnath** in 2022.
 
• Adi Shankaracharya was an 8th-century Indian philosopher and theologian who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta.
 
• The statue is located at the Kedarnath Temple, one of the holiest Hindu shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• This statue is part of a redevelopment project aimed at restoring and improving the Kedarnath temple complex.
 
• The unveiling of the statue is seen as a significant step in preserving and promoting India's spiritual heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kedarnath** is located in the Indian state of Uttarakhand and is part of the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit.
 
• The temple is situated at an altitude of 3,583 meters (11,755 feet) above sea level, near the Chorabari Glacier, the source of the Mandakini river.
 
• Kedarnath Temple was originally built by the Pandavas and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, the holiest Hindu shrines of Lord Shiva.
 
• The region around Kedarnath is prone to natural disasters; in 2013, it was severely affected by flash floods, leading to extensive damage and loss of lives.
 
• Since then, significant efforts have been made to rebuild and restore the temple and its surroundings, ensuring safety and accessibility for pilgrims.

questions.question: An image of which of the following elements is shown by the map of Cyprus from which the element got its name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The element **Copper** is symbolized by the map of Cyprus.
 
• The name **Copper** is derived from the Latin word *Cyprium*, meaning "metal of Cyprus."
 
• In ancient times, Cyprus was a major source of copper, which was extensively mined and traded.
 
• Copper is a highly conductive metal used in electrical wiring, plumbing, and various other applications.
 
• It is also an essential trace element necessary for the survival of all living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper** has the chemical symbol **Cu** and atomic number 29.
 
• It is known for its reddish-orange color and high thermal and electrical conductivity.
 
• Copper has been used by humans for at least 10,000 years, with evidence of its use dating back to ancient civilizations.
 
• The element is found in various ores, including chalcopyrite, bornite, and malachite.
 
• Modern-day applications of copper include electrical equipment, construction materials, and industrial machinery.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by which Ministry of Government of India?

options.text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by the **Ministry of Rural Development** of the Government of India.
 
• The initiative aims to provide livelihood opportunities to the returnee migrant workers and similarly affected rural citizens due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• It focuses on the creation of infrastructure and employment in rural areas, thereby enhancing economic activities.
 
• This Abhiyaan covers 116 districts across 6 states, ensuring a broad reach to the affected populace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The PMGKRA was launched on **20th June 2020** as a part of the economic response to COVID-19.
 
• The Abhiyaan involves the convergence of 25 different types of works/activities, which will provide employment to the workers.
 
• It aims to saturate villages with public infrastructure and create livelihood opportunities in the wake of the pandemic.
 
• It is a 125-day campaign with an estimated budget of **Rs. 50,000 crore**.

questions.question: Who is the first female classical dancer in Indian history to be nominated as a Member of Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rukmini Devi Arundale**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was the first female classical dancer in Indian history to be nominated as a Member of Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• She was nominated in recognition of her significant contributions to Indian classical dance, particularly Bharatanatyam.
 
• Rukmini Devi was instrumental in reviving and popularizing Bharatanatyam, which had fallen into disrepute during the colonial period.
 
• She established the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai, which became a premier institution for training in Bharatanatyam and other classical arts.
 
• Her nomination to the Rajya Sabha marked a significant recognition of the arts in the political sphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rukmini Devi Arundale was born on February 29, 1904, and passed away on February 24, 1986.
 
• She was also a theosophist and an animal rights activist, advocating for vegetarianism and compassion towards animals.
 
• In addition to her work in dance, she was involved in education and was a member of the Indian Parliament from 1952 to 1962.
 
• Rukmini Devi received numerous awards, including the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967.
 
• Her legacy continues to inspire dancers and cultural practitioners in India and around the world.

questions.question: What does the term ‘Overdraft’ mean in banking?

options.text: The process of transferring funds between bank accounts
The maximum withdrawal limit from an ATM

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Short-term financing facility**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Short-term financing facility** is what the term 'Overdraft' means in banking.
 
• An overdraft allows an account holder to withdraw more money than what is available in their bank account.
 
• It is a type of short-term loan provided by banks to help cover temporary cash shortfalls.
 
• The bank charges interest on the overdrawn amount, and there may also be fees associated with the overdraft facility.
 
• Overdrafts are useful for managing cash flow and unexpected expenses, ensuring that transactions are not declined due to insufficient funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The interest rate on an overdraft can be higher compared to other types of loans.
 
• Overdraft limits are typically set by the bank based on the customer's creditworthiness and account history.
 
• Exceeding the overdraft limit can result in additional penalties and higher interest rates.
 
• It is important for account holders to monitor their account balances regularly to avoid excessive overdraft fees.
 
• Some banks offer overdraft protection services, which link the primary account to another account or line of credit to cover overdrafts.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the literacy rate recorded in Kerala?
questions.solution:

• The first Census of India was conducted in **1871**.
 
• The Census provides critical data that helps in planning and policy-making at both the state and national levels.
 
• Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged 7 and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• In the 2011 Census, the overall literacy rate in India was recorded at **74.04%**.
 
• Kerala has consistently maintained a high literacy rate due to its focus on universal education and adult literacy programs.

questions.question: Janmashtami is a Hindu festival that celebrates the birth (janma) of the god, Krishna on the eighth (ashtami) day of the dark fortnight of the Hindu month of _____________.
questions.solution:

• **Janmashtami** is a significant Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Krishna.

• Krishna's birth is celebrated at midnight, the time when it is believed he was born.
 
• Various rituals include **Rasa Lila** (dramatic enactments of Krishna's life) and **Dahi Handi** (breaking of the pot filled with curd) which are popular in Maharashtra.
 
• Janmashtami is also an occasion to reflect on the teachings of Krishna, especially those found in the **Bhagavad Gita**.

questions.question: What is the tenure of the Vice-President of India?

options.text: Until he wants to hold the office

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tenure of the Vice-President of India is **5 years**.
 
• The Vice-President can be re-elected for subsequent terms.
 
• The Vice-President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• In case of any vacancy due to death, resignation, or removal, the election to fill the vacancy must be held as soon as possible.
 
• The Vice-President may continue to hold office until his successor assumes charge, even if his term has expired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• The election is conducted through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Vice-President can be removed from office by a resolution passed by an effective majority in the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
 
• Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President of India, serving from 1952 to 1962.
 
• The Vice-President acts as the President in the absence of the President due to death, resignation, impeachment, or otherwise.
